chapter: Los Angeles 1947-48, Rock Island and bebop in New York
title: His view that bop was made to exclude jam-session players
summary: He argues that bop's changed harmonies were meant to stop outsiders from stealing Black music.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: -- was writing for Benny Goodman, making him a swing band, you know, like Edgar Sampson and Jimmy Mundy, they were writing all these swing arrangements for Benny Goodman. And down on 52nd Street they was letting the Caucasians come and sit in, you know, trying to steal our music. And a lot of them did.
Well, what do you think should have been done? Bop? The augmentation?
Yes. But no-one else should have been allowed to get on the bandstand, in order to cut out these jam sessions, you know, and let people learn the true black form.
This is the American true art form.
-- the bop -- so-called bop revolution was --
It was strictly conceived to eliminate people from jam sessions?
That was the only reason for --
Especially there at Minton's Playhouse where they were working.
And that was the only -- the sole reason for the new music?
